coreIdea: Regular = finite-state recognizable. Needs unbounded counting/matching (a^n b^n, palindrome) → NOT regular. Bounded/modular counting → IS regular.
mustRememberFormulas: Closed under: ∪, ∩, complement, concat, star, reversal
Minimal DFA states = number of Myhill-Nerode equivalence classes
Every finite language is regular; not every subset of a regular language is regular

patternRecognitionTable.seeThis: specific language defined, asked 'is it regular'
operation (union/intersection/prefix/half) asked if it preserves regularity
'minimum DFA states' or given k-state minimal DFA, reason about L
'strongest TRUE statement' about a finite language, or subset-checking algorithm

commonTrapsQuickList: Bounded/modular counting (mod k, or 'exactly k more') IS regular; unbounded matching is NOT
Every finite subset is regular ALWAYS; not every subset of an infinite regular set is regular
Infinite union of regular languages is NOT guaranteed regular — only finite unions
NFA states ≠ minimal DFA states — subset construction gives an upper bound (2^n), not the exact minimum
highYieldPyqLessons: Classification (14/35) and closure properties (13/35) together are ~77% of this topic — these two skills carry almost the whole topic.
This is the conceptual bedrock for all of TOC — every later topic (FA, RE, CFL, Decidability) reuses this regular-vs-not judgment repeatedly.
